rules.title: Thin reference layout
rules.statement: A thin reference (plain `&T`/`&mut T`/`*T`/fn-ptr to a Sized pointee) occupies one machine pointer: {size=8, align=8}.

rules.title: Fat reference layout
rules.statement: Every fat reference — slice `&[T]`/`str`, trait object `&dyn Tr`, closure value, custom-DST ref, and zone-mut ref — is a two-word pair of {size=16, align=8}.

rules.title: Slice fat pair = {data,len}
rules.statement: A slice value (`&[T]`, `str`) is the pair {data: ptr, len: i64}.

rules.title: Trait object fat pair = {data,vtable}
rules.statement: A trait object value (`dyn Tr`) is the pair {data_ptr, vtable_ptr}; a `&dyn` value is a pointer to this 16-byte storage.

rules.title: Closure value = {fn,env}
rules.statement: A closure value is the pair {fn_ptr, env_ptr}, 16 bytes.

rules.title: Relative-offset reference layout
rules.statement: A relative-offset (self-relative) reference is stored as a single i64 offset word: {size=8, align=8}.
rules.divergence: Logos self-relative pointers (zoned/Writ); no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Fat-ref struct/enum field stored inline
rules.statement: When a fat reference (slice, `dyn`/`Box<dyn>`, closure, custom-DST ref) is a payload field of an enum variant, it is stored inline as its full 16-byte fat pair, never collapsed to an 8-byte handle; thin refs keep the by-value 8-byte pointer.

rules.title: Enum payload members stored by value
rules.statement: Enum variant payload members are laid out by value: each member contributes its full by-value layout (e.g. `Option<&[u8]>` payload = the 16-byte slice fat pair), unlike struct/tuple fields which may store a slice/closure/tuple as an 8-byte ptr.

rules.title: Variant payload laid out as a struct
rules.statement: A variant's payload is laid out exactly like a struct/tuple of its fields, including inter-field alignment padding; a multi-field variant's payload size is the aligned aggregate, not the naive sum of field sizes (e.g. `Cons{head:i32, tail:*const List}` = 16, not 12).

rules.title: Enum payload size/align = max over variants
rules.statement: A tagged enum's payload byte size is the maximum payload size over all variants, and its payload alignment is the maximum payload alignment over all variants.

rules.title: Unit `()` payload field omitted
rules.statement: A `()` (Void) payload field of an enum variant contributes no field and no bytes to the variant payload.

rules.title: Null-pointer niche for Option<&T>-shape
rules.statement: A two-variant enum with one fieldless variant and one single-field variant whose field is `&T`/`&mut T` is pointer-sized (8 bytes, no separate discriminant word): the discriminant is encoded as null vs non-null at offset 0, since references are guaranteed non-null.

rules.title: Null-pointer niche for #[non_null] 8-byte wrapper
rules.statement: The null-pointer niche also applies when the single-field variant's field is a `#[non_null]` struct that is exactly an 8-byte pointer wrapper (Box/Rc/Arc-shape), whose invariant guarantees offset-0 is non-zero.
rules.divergence: Logos `#[non_null]` attribute exposes Rust's NonNull niche to user wrapper types.

rules.title: Low-bit niche packs pointer + small-int arms
rules.statement: A two single-field-arm enum where one arm is a pointer to an align>=2 pointee (low bit always 0) and the other arm is a <=56-bit integer stored shifted `(v<<1)|1` packs into one word; the discriminant is the low bit (0=ptr arm, 1=int arm).
rules.divergence: Logos low-bit pointer-tagging niche; no direct Rust analog.

rules.title: Zoned (#[zoned2]) raw 64-bit low-bit niche
rules.statement: In a `#[zoned2]` enum, the low-bit niche additionally accepts a raw `*T` pointer arm (trusting the zone allocator's >=2 alignment even for `*u8`) and a raw 64-bit `u64`/`i64` value arm stored without a `<<1` shift (the producer bakes the low-bit-1 tag into the word).
rules.divergence: Logos zoned (Writ) niche; no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Low-bit niche integer arm widths
rules.statement: Eligible low-bit-niche value arms are Bool(1), I8/U8(8), I16/U16(16), I24/U24(24), I32/U32(32), I56(56) packed shifted; I64/U64(64) qualify only as the raw zoned variant.

rules.title: Tuple element aggregate types stored inline
rules.statement: A tuple element whose type is a struct, enum, slice (incl. `str`), closure, trait object (`&dyn`), or nested tuple is stored inline as its full by-value layout (e.g. struct footprint, 16-byte fat pair), never collapsed to an 8-byte pointer.

rules.title: Ref-to-tuple resolves inner tuple layout
rules.statement: A `&(T,U)`/`&mut (T,U)`/`*(T,U)` resolves to the layout of the inner tuple `(T,U)` (default binding modes for tuple patterns over ref scrutinees).

rules.title: Generic enum concrete name mangling
rules.statement: A generic enum instantiation's concrete name is `EnumName` followed by `__<mangle(arg)>` for each type argument, where struct/datatype args mangle via concrete-struct-name and others via their type string.

rules.title: dyn/slice/zone-mut returned by 16B value
rules.statement: When returned by value, a trait object, slice, or zone-mut fat reference is materialized as its full 16-byte storage pair in the caller's frame; closure, custom-DST, thin, and rel-offset references are returned as their 8-byte value (pointer/word).
